newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stock drop but busy trade in parallel market.
newsitem.headline: Amman stock drop but busy trade in parallel market.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell on Tuesday despite some activity on the parallel market amid a wait-and-see mood among institutional investors depressing overall trade, dealers said.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.32 percent to 152.77 points in low turnover of 305,331 dinars ($431,258) with volume in the parallel market which lists newly established firms overtaking the official bourse.

Only a handful of stock saw activity in otherwise quiet trade in the official market dominated by some speculative deals by local investors as institutional investors continue to steer away from the bourse in the absence of new market direction.
But moderate activity in the parallel market on firms such as Middle East Complex, a manufacturer of South Korean Goldstar products under license, helped inject some movement into the quiet market.
Deals on NAMICO, which manufactures engineering products, and portfolio investment house Arab Financial Investments helped to cushion the overall market, dealers said.
NAMICO rose 0.03 dinars to 0.68 dinars in 6,556 dinars worth of trade.
But heaviest traded was Middle East Complex in a bloc deal on 586,100 shares worth 457,158 dinars. Arab Financial Investment rose 0.02 dinars to 0.51 dinars in trade worth 35,429 dinars.

Recent political uncertainty over the fate of Middle East peace combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.21 dinars to 81.03 points, 2.84 percent down from the start of the year.
